paragraphs: A recent study has revealed a gloomy mood among young people in Turkey, and has shown that nearly two-thirds are considering emigrating, primarily toward Europe.

Under President Erdogan’s rule, democracy is increasingly restricted, which leads to fears of political repression. Young artists face severe censorship, as the authorities regularly cancel performances over critical lyrics. In addition, the country is suffering from high inflation and a stagnant economy. This leaves young Turks with bad job prospects and an official unemployment rate of 31%. While some students move abroad to Belgium or France to find a stable career, others choose to stay. Some describe themselves as patriotic and conservative, and they support the government’s actions.
Turkey now faces a danger of losing its youth as young people choose between staying to fight for freedom or seeking success abroad.

words.d: when a government uses police, power, or strict rules to control people by force and take away their freedom
the official act of controlling and stopping speech, music, or writing that the government doesn’t like

paragraphs: The mood among young people in Turkey is very sad and hopeless. A new study shows that nearly 64% of young Turks want to leave their country and move to Europe.

There are two main reasons for this. First, they feel they don’t have freedom of expression. The government is very strict, and the police often censor artists, musicians, and comedians. Second, the economy is in a bad situation. Inflation is very high, and more than 30% of young people cannot find a job. Some students are already moving to countries like France and Belgium for university.
But not everyone wants to go. Some young people love their country and prefer to stay and work hard in Istanbul, even if life is difficult. Turkey is now in danger of losing its young generation.

words.d: feeling that a bad situation will never get better
the legal right to speak, write, create art, or share your opinions openly
to examine books, music, or news and take away parts which speak badly about the government

paragraphs: Many young people in Turkey are not happy today. The economy is bad, and it is very difficult to find a job. In fact, many young people do not have work or go to school. Life is also very expensive because everything costs a lot of money.

Many young Turks want to leave their country and live in Europe. They want to find a better future and speak freely. Now, they are afraid to speak. Musicians and students say that the government checks and stops their work. Some students are moving to France to study.
But some young people want to stay because they love their country. The situation is difficult. We will see what happens next.

words.d: how money and products move within a country
when something costs a lot of money
